title: apricity-daw collection.rs: a drum rack of the collection's short sounds via an in-memory drum kit
description:
## Intent

The collection's short sounds as a drum rack, using the compiler for level matching so the pads sit exactly as Apricity would level them.

## Scope

- `crates/apricity-daw/src/collection.rs`: build an in-memory `Score` (tempo 120, key of the first item, no tracks) with one clip per short item (`source` = sample path, `saved` = clip name) and a drum kit `<collection>` whose pads are named after the clips (made unique with `-2` when two items share a name), in collection order; compile it with the library loader (`apricity_data::loader::make`); pass `Timeline.kits` (M1, apricitus-c74565) to M1's rack writer with an explicit pad order (collection order from C1, not the drum-word table).
- "Short" = one bar or less of the item's own beat grid (seconds for an unwarped sample: at most 2 s); the limit is one constant, per the owner's decision.

## Verification

```sh
CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 safe-run.sh -- cargo test -p apricity-daw --test conformance
```
The rack scenarios of `features/daw/collection-folder.feature` pass.

## Release

`feat(<this task id>): a collection's short sounds as a drum rack`. Not breaking.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the numbered-clip-files task and by M1's rack writer (apricitus-f3ea55); the explicit pad order may need a small option on that writer.
